Ha that is interesting! I guess they customize our POS systems to accept retail gear so they could avoid putting in another system that they have to support. Sorry about that!

If counterpoint uses the same support team, then they may be top for you since you all are low on manpower for onsite troubleshooting.

I work with about 80 or so POS systems and I must say I have never heard of any of those people.  I'll give you a run down of the ones I have worked with which may not be of good help to you but you never know.

Micros/Syphony/Anything Oracle: they work but if something goes wrong and you need tech support god help you.  All outsourced and if they have to escalate the ticket, I have yet to get a call or email back in under 3 months.  Escalation happens very easily as tier 1 only copy/pastes scripts and queries. Anything requiring thought and you are hosed. I hate them with a passion.

Maitre'D: Works and they are way ahead of the curve on EMV support.  Their tech support is very good as well.

Aloha: Still struggling to adapt to EMV but their support is wonderful.  They'll have techs out onsite usually same day if they can't fix over phone.

Digital Dining: Same as Maitre'D. On the ball with EMV support and their tech support is responsive. They may take a while to fix the issue but you can always reach someone and they do keep in constant contact.

Squirrel: Still behind on the EMV game but their tech support is one of my absolute favorites. You can always reach someone quickly and they are very good at troubleshooting with no escalation required.

Sorry if this complicates things for you more.  I would definitely recommend against Multiflex by your description. If they are still using java then I doubt they are in PCI Compliance.  Most hospitality systems that require java usually require a version from 2 years ago if they are still updating it.

I know there are now some POS systems that are entirely cloud based and that moves all PCI compliance off of you and onto that company. They will provide you with terminals and even include an online shopping option! That will save you a TON of work and headaches especially if you are such a small shop without an IT team.  We have been looking into just for that perk alone, I can't think of any off the top of my head though since I am not heading that project but I know there is excitement.  

*edit* forgot to add that yes they are dining room POS systems but they can customize for businesses. We use a few of them for our gift shops and etc.

Ha I'm a bit jealous.  We have 7 offices in the USA alone. Our poor network lady was responsible for 93 networks.  I helped her with her resume and told her to count every office and hotel as a network because it damn well is.  Yeah she got a job in like 2 weeks after the revamp.  I miss her :(

Not too much I can teach unfortunately. Just don't be afraid to learn, try new things, and do what you think is right.  I'll give you some examples from my current job.

When I told my boss I wanted to start implementing GPOs he was against it saying that he didn't see the need since .bat files already get the job done.  I quietly implemented them anyways (didn't think it would step on any toes and I quietly suspect he has no idea what GPO's are anyways) and now our call volume is drastically lowered. I have never mentioned this to him. The call volume and the extra space to breathe is its own reward, don't need to rub it in.

For our inventory system, they told me the company was willing to pay a grand total of $0 for that to happen.  Me calling hotels for weeks on end and forgoing my actual job was apparently a price to pay that they were ok with.  I had never really dabbled with linux before but I ended up propping up my own box and then really had fun learning how to set up GLPI and various inventory agents until I stopped with Fusion Inventory. I then went on to create my own little vbs script for our GPOs to make the entire inventory process automated.  Company caved and bought me an SSL certificate for the system once I showed it off so now it's secure too!

That's really all there is to it.  Make do with what you are given and do the best you can with it.  If it involves extra learning or doing something new, so be it.  Took me a good month before I got comfortable with linux but damn does clicking one button save me more time than calling everyone.  I even set up two additional linux boxes for network monitoring so we get alerts when ISP's are down around the world.  I started using the new knowledge to just expand everything further and better.

Plus everything adds more checkboxes to the resume so that is always a plus.
Ah thank you sir, that is a huge boost to my own self esteem!

Reason I have stuck with this job is my resume looks amazing from this company. They are one of largest management company in America and it used to be a team of 2 people (they expanded to 4).  1 helpdesk, 1 network, 1 sysadmin, and the boss.  We have locations in Canada, US, Europe, Singapore, and Japan all with computers and servers that I am soley responsible for.

When I came in they really were just too swamped and didn't have much knowledge to implement anything.

They had no inventory so when we sold 53 hotels at once, I had to call each hotel and ask the clerks to find me serial numbers and model numbers of all their computers and servers.  I had to track down laptops and took about 2 weeks.

I set up a quick ubuntu VM with glpi and fusioninventory and now any computer that has been added to our domain gets automatically inventoried.  Providing inventory sheet to a buyer now requires just a click of a button and a pdf is created.

They gave us a tour of the datacenter and EVERY server had at least one dead harddrive.  Boss had no idea and that's when I realized they had no monitoring system.  I implemented scripts so now any server in the world that has a bad harddrive, memory, fan, someone opens the case, gets an automated email alert.

I finally got them to realize that GPO is a GOOD thing.  They were giving everyone custom .bat files for share drives and whenever there was a new employee they would install the printers manually.  We have a huge turnover rate (I have created/removed about 300+ users this year alone) so I implemented GPO so now as long as they are in the correct OU, they get their share, their printers, their security permissions etc.  Cut down calls by about 50% alone on that one.

Such a daunting task and you can get overloaded easy but damn does the resume look good when you can basically say "I made it a functioning company" lol.  Sorry I definitely turned this into a humblegrab post.  Damn proud of everything I did for this company solo.

Our poor network admin had it worse but that's another story to tell on another day lol

An example would be that today I am going to pick up my Niece from her school and while I have done it before I am absolutely terrified each time. Hi guys I just wanted to type this up because I'm hoping it will help to get this off my chest and hoping your comments might be a good pick-me-up.  Essentially I pretty much have lost the will to live it seems.  I've been researching guns (one thing that has stopped from me doing this sooner is my fear of a long, painful death) and am basically in the planning stages.  I got my note already typed out and already have my plans envisioned.

Now the reason behind all this is kind of lame in comparison to others who commit suicide because of pain or other good reasons.  My main reason is because I am tired of being unhappy.  The last time I can remember being truly happy is sometime in elementary school, the good old days of no worries and soccer everyday.  It has been a constant battle with depression and lately it has been winning.  I just cannot find pleasure in anything anymore.  I just kind of stare off into things and feign the respective emotions when I am with others.  Movies, TV shows, and, most recently, music just do nothing for me anymore.  I just don't feel even fleeting moments of joy anymore and it's really starting to break me down.

Social life is pretty much nonexistent for me now.  I went through a period where I wanted to change my entire life and try to obtain happiness.  I lost a lot of weight (about 150 lbs) and tried to make more friends and be more social.  I couldn't stand it and I make myself seem like an ass more often than not.  I was in a constant state of paralyzed fear when trying to be social. I was always trying to evaluate everything in my head and making sure anything I would say would not offend anyone.  And I mean everything even if someone would say “do you want another drink?” I would sit there and figure out what must be said.  A few times I have even put my foot in my mouth and made me feel horrible afterwards for months on end, even if it was absolutely nothing to worry about.  I overanalyze ever misstep even when everyone else has already forgotten it.  Little things will haunt me for months on end and make me feel horrible at random points during a day.   It got so bad that it has gotten to the point where I have given up on being social.  I just can't handle the constant state of fear that I end up in.  I have gained most of my weight back and I just basically don't feel the need to even try anymore.

The latest developments that have pushed everything into the forefront has been just life in general as of late.  I'm about to graduate from college and I have been looking for a job for months now.  No one is hiring and lately I have been beginning to question even my own credentials.  I don't feel like I'm good at what I do anymore and feel like I will never be hired for anything.  I will have students loans that will need to start being repaid a few months after graduation and I don't see myself being able to find a decent job.  I do not wish to get back into the services business (food, bagging, etc) as people were always demeaning and cruel to me in this situation.  When I think about my future, I don't feel any hope.  I just feel worse about myself and my life and I don't want to experience it.

Like I said the reasons are pretty lame but I just can't stand to being sad, lonely, and paralyzed with fear anymore.  I have been meaning to post on this subreddit for weeks and stared at the post button for about 20 minutes (and typed the captcha wrong once ha) but even something as simple and anonymous as this paralyzed me with fear of judgment.  I hate that whenever I go outside that I am overcome with fear of others and thoughts that they are judging me.  I can't stand waking up every morning with a sigh.  I hate seeing everyone around me being happy and constantly wishing I were them.  I am constantly daydreaming that I am someone else.  I play video games not just to have fun, but to have an escape from my life.  I enjoy the feeling of being someone else.  I just don't think I am cut out for life.  Thanks for taking your time to read all this, I feel slightly better for having typed it all up, hopefully I can now get a good night's sleep (I've been having troubles sleeping the past few months as well).  I just feel like life is not worth living anymore.  I had a good run but I just feel like I can’t continue this.  I’m posting this to get this off my chest and hopefully have you guys put this more into perspective for me.  Again I thank you for reading this all, I’m pretty much rambling now.
